question: A café started the morning with 155 cups of coffee sold. By midmorning, 23 more cups were sold. At midday, a catering order required the café to prepare 3 times that morning total. Since the café measures coffee grounds in ounces but sells drinks by the cup, the barista kept a conversion chart on the wall. In the afternoon, a citywide event required 8 times that midday total. By evening, 13 more cups were sold at a pop-up stand. How many cups had the café sold by evening?

A coach tracked athlete metrics. Starting with 30 athletes, recruitment multiplied by 5 (150 athletes). Late registrations added 33 (183 athletes). Team selection multiplied by 4 (732 athletes). Competition cuts removed 403 (329 athletes). Final roster reductions removed 257 athletes. Triple the final would represent the conference total. How many final athletes?

A business starts with 142 items in inventory. They add 63 items from production. They add 40 items from suppliers. They multiply by 7 to forecast for 7 weeks. They add 40 more items from recovery. They multiply by 9 to project quarterly. Converting to units, what is their quarterly projection?

Two shop owners, Elif and Bram, track their sock inventory, but this story follows only Elif's stock, which started at 186 pairs, more than Bram's stock. A bulk order left her with 3 times as many pairs. A supplier added 73 more pairs. A big sale then used up 591 pairs. A late shipment added 14 more pairs, and a final small delivery added 5 more, around the time a rival shop priced its socks at 6 dollars a pair, unrelated to Elif's count. How many pairs of socks did Elif have in the end?

A packing house's bin held 240 apples at the start of the morning, though the manager mentioned a completely unrelated order of 10,000 apples destined for a different client entirely. Workers picked 20 more apples and tossed them into the same bin. To fill a large export order, the crew multiplied the bin's contents ninefold by matching every apple with eight more from cold storage. That export batch was then split evenly across five delivery trucks, and only the lead truck's load is tracked from here. The lead truck's apples were further divided evenly onto six pallets for the warehouse, and only one of those pallets continued to the final buyer. Finally, 23 apples from a late harvest were added to that pallet. How many apples were on the pallet after the late harvest was added?

In the morning Ed's stall had 91 pies on the counter, but 6 pies were dropped and 68 pies were sold. In the afternoon Ed baked until he had 6 times as many pies as were left, and his mother brought 23 more pies from home. In the evening his brother matched the stock exactly, so Ed had 2 times as many pies as before. How many pies does Ed have now?

A factory produced 123 units initially. They multiplied by 5 for a large order. They removed 432 units for returns. They multiplied by 4 for packaging lots. They removed 589 for a canceled contract. They removed 88 more in adjustments. They removed 34 for quality control. The facility had 25 workers. How many units remained?
A builder had 52 bricks. He multiplied by 4. He added 19 more. He removed 175. He divided by 4. He multiplied by 2. A neighboring site has 300 bricks separately. How many bricks?

A vending company's coin box had $50 in it, equal to 5,000 cents on the accounting sheet. A slot-machine style promotion multiplied the box ninefold for the grand opening. Maintenance costs then used up $295. A customer's returned deposit added $12. The company then paid out $159 for a parts repair. A regional bonus multiplied the remaining balance fivefold, and a final matching grant multiplied it fourfold again. How much money was in the coin box at the end?

Marcus assembles 75 badges every hour at the workshop, and last Friday he worked for 9 hours straight. He packed the whole day's output into 3 identical crates, with the same number of badges in each crate. Dana, who runs the sister workshop, ordered 6 crates of exactly that size for a conference. The two of them joked that Dana's single order was larger than anything Marcus had ever built in a day. Sadly, 254 badges in Dana's order came out with the wrong logo and were thrown away. The workshop has been open for 12 years. How many usable badges were in Dana's order?

A gardener managed plant inventory. He started with 63 seedlings. He multiplied by 9 for the spring planting. Then 76 seedlings wilted and were removed. A late frost damaged 466 more seedlings. But 40 replacement seedlings arrived. He recorded inventory morning, afternoon, and evening. How many healthy seedlings remain?

Nia had 166 stickers and gave 100 of them to her friend Ravi, who then had more stickers than Nia. She bought 26 stickers at the shop. Then she bought a matching sticker for every one she owned, so she had 2 of each. She used 32 stickers on her notebook and gave 73 to her little brother. How many stickers does Nia have now?

Priya's project has 74 weeks, and 57 weeks are done. She writes the rest in days, at 7 days to a week, then takes 16 days off for holidays and adds 23 days for a client extension. The team has 9 members. She splits the days equally into 6 sprints. How many days does each sprint have?
A manufacturer had 106 items. They multiplied by 4 times. They multiplied by 5 times. They multiplied by 5 times. They added 44 items. David had fewer items. Maria had more. How many items?

A tiling firm had 237 boxes of slate in its yard and bought 8 more from a shop that was closing. Every box holds 4 tiles. A driver added 7 loose tiles that had been rattling about in his van. The whole stock was then shared equally between 3 building sites. Each tile delivered to the first site weighs 7 kilograms, and 33 kilograms of broken pieces were later swept up and carted away from that site. The firm bills its labour in minutes rather than hours. How many kilograms of slate does the first site have left?

In the morning a printing press ran for 7 minutes at 106 pages per minute, and then did a second run of exactly the same length, making 2 runs in all. In the afternoon 35 extra pages were printed and added, making up one full job. In the evening the manager confirmed that 5 identical jobs are printed every day, and that the press will run for 9 days. She also adds 27 sample pages to the final total. How many pages will be printed in total?

A candy factory packs 240 pounds of chocolate into crates today, in a plant that also stores 500 pounds of unrelated sugar syrup. The batch is split evenly among 3 delivery trucks, and only one truck's load is tracked from here. That truck's load is then split evenly again among 4 store routes, and only one route's share continues. At the first stop, 14 pounds are set aside as samples. A wholesale bonus then multiplies what's left by 9, a stretch of packing that takes 180 minutes, or three hours. Finally, 29 more pounds are added from a late top-up delivery. How many pounds of chocolate does that route have now?

A mail-order company sent out 43 parcels of books in the first week, and 1 of them was lost by the carrier and written off. The following week it despatched 61 more parcels. The delivery van covers 90 kilometres on its round. Every parcel that arrived safely contained 5 books, and half of the titles were paperbacks. The warehouse then added 65 single books that had been ordered without a parcel. Each book on the invoice is priced at 8 dollars, and the invoice is written in dollars rather than in cents. What is the total price in dollars?
A production line made 231 items initially. This was multiplied by 3. Then multiplied by 8. He added 65. This was multiplied by 6 for monthly production. What was the final item count?

A farm had 232 carrots. They added 53 carrots from a second harvest. They multiplied by 4 for a restaurant order. They divided by 5 to allocate to five locations. Finally, 18 more carrots were added. Using a morning-to-evening production timeline, how many carrots are in the final allocation?

A decorating warehouse keeps all of its wallpaper rolls in one bay. The bay held 236 rolls, and a returned order added 13 more. The manager then ordered enough for the bay to hold 9 times as many rolls as it did. A national contract made the bay hold 4 times that number. Half of the rolls in the bay are patterned. A supplier finally added 17 sample rolls to the same bay. How many rolls are in the bay now?

A jam factory packed 222 boxes with 4 jars in every box, and the sample room added 74 loose jars to the store. A supermarket order then took 698 jars away, and 60 jars came back when another order was cancelled. Each jar in the store holds 9 spoonfuls of jam. The factory chimney is 30 metres tall. The recipe book is written in grams rather than in kilograms. How many spoonfuls of jam are in the store?

A farmer had 23 eggs. She removed 10 eggs for cooking. Then removed 10 more. Finally, she removed 2 more. She multiplied her remaining eggs by 4 for a breeding program. Then multiplied by 9 again. How many eggs does she have now?

A team scored 111 points. They added 15 points. They multiplied by 9 for a tournament. They divided by 3 for three divisions. They added 20 points in overtime. They multiplied by 5 for final ranking. What was the final score per division?

A student had 58 pages. They divided in half to 29. They multiplied by 5 to 145. They removed 53, leaving 92. They multiplied by 5 to 460. They removed 322, leaving 138. They removed 86 more, leaving 52 pages. How many pages remain?
